metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to 'multiple low quality pull requests' and AI generated comments, reviews, issues, or pull requests posted without a good understanding of the content
domains.accountability_wording: users submitting multiple low quality pull requests, or AI generated comments, reviews, issues, or pull requests... might be banned from the organisation

evidence.quote: Opening AI generated pull requests w/o understanding them;

users submitting multiple low quality pull requests, or AI generated comments, reviews, issues, or pull requests, where the user does not show a good understanding of what they are posting, might be banned

domains.reasoning: The CoC directly names AI-generated pull requests and comments/issues as regulated content: they are permitted only if the submitter shows understanding, otherwise the submitter risks being banned from the organisation. This states both a supervision expectation (human understanding of AI output) and ties the ban consequence to the contributor who posted it, so accountability is assigned to the contributor.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level; no scope limit; no accountability holder named
domains.reasoning: The Code of Conduct never discusses meeting recording, transcription, or notetaker/meeting bots in any form.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level; no accountability holder for docs/blog/design AI use
domains.reasoning: The document mentions 'improving the documentation' only as a general example of valuable non-code contribution, with no reference to AI use in documentation, blogs, or design assets.

domains.rationale_only_mention: Due to the burden put on maintainers, users submitting multiple low quality pull requests, or AI generated comments, reviews, issues, or pull requests...
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI used to take moderation actions; no accountability holder
domains.reasoning: The policy cites maintainer burden as the reason for banning low-quality/AI-generated submissions, which is a rationale about moderation workload, not a rule about AI being used to perform moderation actions itself. No supervision level or accountability holder for AI-driven moderation is stated.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to AI generated reviews left by users without a good understanding of what they are posting
domains.accountability_wording: users submitting ... AI generated comments, reviews, issues, or pull requests ... might be banned from the organisation

evidence.quote: or AI generated comments, reviews, issues, or pull requests, where the user does not show a good understanding of what they are posting, might be banned

domains.reasoning: AI-generated reviews are explicitly named alongside comments, issues, and pull requests as content that must be understood by the person posting it, with the same ban consequence and contributor-level accountability as the code_contributions clause.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level; no accountability holder for agentic/autonomous use
domains.reasoning: There is no mention of agents or autonomous AI systems acting on the repository independent of a human submitter.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level; no rule on energy/water/carbon impact
domains.reasoning: The Code of Conduct does not discuss energy, water, or carbon footprint of AI tools; the only external reference is a linked blog post title, which is not itself policy text asserting an environmental rationale within this document.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level; no rule on server load or hardware cost
domains.reasoning: No statement addresses server load, hardware cost, or financing burden from AI tooling; the document's stated burden concerns are about maintainer review time (moderation), not infrastructure.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on project data being used to train models
domains.reasoning: The Code of Conduct never addresses whether scikit-learn's own issues, discussions, or user data may be used to train AI models; its AI content concerns copyright/quality of AI-generated submissions, not outbound use of project data.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: The Code of Conduct addresses AI narrowly and only through a single 'Low Quality and AI Generated Contributions Policy' clause: it conditions AI-generated pull requests, issues, comments, and reviews on the submitter demonstrating genuine understanding, threatening organisation-wide bans for violators, but is silent on notetaker bots, content/documentation, AI-driven moderation, autonomous agents, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and use of project data for training.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
